meta.location: Zarahemla, the land southward, and the line at Bountiful
meta.unit: The rise of the Gadianton band (Helaman 1–6)
principles: Dissenters who leave and come back armed

world_behind.title: The chapter covers nine years
world_behind.text: Verse 1 opens in the fifty-fourth year and verse 18 reaches the sixty-second, with each stage dated.

world_behind.title: The rebellion starts inside the church
world_behind.text: Verse 1 names dissensions in the church and contention among the people, with much bloodshed.

world_behind.title: The exiles recruit the Lamanites twice
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has the first attempt refused, and verse 4 has a second group succeeding two years later.

world_behind.title: All the land southward is lost
world_behind.text: Verse 5 has Zarahemla taken by the fifty-eighth year, and verse 8 credits the loss to Nephite dissenters with Lamanite armies.

world_behind.title: The line at Bountiful is a day's journey
world_behind.text: Verse 7 measures the fortified front from the west sea to the east as one day's travel for a Nephite.

world_behind.title: Recovery follows preaching
world_behind.text: Verses 14 through 16 have Moronihah, Nephi, and Lehi preaching, the people repenting, and half the land coming back.

world_behind.title: The armies are now evenly matched
world_behind.text: Verse 26 says Lamanite strength equaled Nephite strength man for man, a reversal of what Alma 43 through 62 assumed.

words.text: Treated at Alma 48:9, of Moroni's system of works. Here the word covers a single continuous line rather than a set of cities, and the record measures it in walking time.
The grinding down of people with less power. The record uses the word three times, twice in quoted Isaiah and once here. Verse 12 makes it the second item in the list of causes.

Loud claims made for oneself. The record uses the word eight times, including Ammon's careful denial at Alma 26:35. Verse 13 turns it on its head: boasting in their own strength, they were left in it.

To risk, to go forward without assurance. The word occurs once in the record and twice in the King James Bible, both of the arrow drawn at a venture that killed Ahab. Moronihah ventures only after the people repent.
To give up entirely. The word occurs once in the record and never in the King James Bible. Verse 19 applies it to the plan to recover the rest of the land.
Without any way around it. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible never. It appears at the hinge of a conditional: cleave to God, or perish.

phrases.term: The rebellious part were slain and driven out of the land, and they did go unto the king of the Lamanites
phrases.text: Exile as policy, and its cost. The men driven out become the men who persuade an enemy army to come.

phrases.term: It being a day's journey for a Nephite, on the line which they had fortified
phrases.text: The record's one measurement of the narrow neck. Mormon gives it as travel time rather than distance.

phrases.term: It was among those also who professed to belong to the church of God
phrases.text: Mormon places the wickedness inside the church as well as outside it. Helaman 3:33 had made the same distinction about pride.

phrases.term: Withholding their food from the hungry, withholding their clothing from the naked
phrases.text: Two items in a list of ten. The list runs from pride through oppression and mockery to murder and desertion, and Mormon gives it as the reason for a military defeat.

phrases.term: Their boastings in their own strength, they were left in their own strength
phrases.text: The sentence turns on itself. The claim and the consequence are the same words, and the result is that they did not prosper.

phrases.term: Inasmuch as they did repent they did begin to prosper
phrases.text: The rule stated in eleven words. Verse 16 has Moronihah acting on it, leading them out only after he saw the repentance.

phrases.term: He did venture to lead them forth from place to place
phrases.text: A commander describing his own campaign as a risk. He recovers half the land, and verse 18 has the advance stopping there.

phrases.term: They had altered and trampled under their feet the laws of Mosiah
phrases.text: The specific charge. Mosiah 29:25 had given laws described as correct and given by the hand of the Lord, and this verse says they had been changed.

phrases.term: The judgments of God did stare them in the face
phrases.text: The image is direct and unblinking. The verse pairs it with a church dwindling and with disbelief in prophecy and revelation.

phrases.term: The Spirit of the Lord doth not dwell in unholy temples
phrases.text: The reason given for the withdrawal. Benjamin had said it of a man in Mosiah 2:37, and Paul says the same of a body in 1 Corinthians 3:16.

phrases.term: The strength of the Lamanites was as great as their strength, even man for man
phrases.text: The measurement that ends the chapter. Twenty chapters of war had turned on Nephite advantage, and Mormon reports the advantage gone in the space of not many years.

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: Dissension and recruitment
verses.text: The fifty-fourth year brings dissensions in the church, contention, and bloodshed. The rebellious part are slain or driven out and go to the Lamanite king. Their first attempt to raise a war fails because the Lamanites are afraid. Two years later a second group succeeds, and a year is spent preparing.

verses.label: v. 5–8
verses.title: The land southward lost
verses.text: The Lamanites come down in the fifty-seventh year, and by the fifty-eighth they hold Zarahemla and every land up to Bountiful. Moronihah's armies are pushed back and fortify a line from the west sea to the east, a day's journey across. Nephite dissenters with Lamanite armies hold everything southward.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: Half recovered
verses.text: In the sixtieth year Moronihah regains many parts and many cities, and by the sixty-first they have half their possessions back.

verses.label: v. 11–13
verses.title: The cause named
verses.text: Mormon says the loss would not have happened except for wickedness, including among church members. He lists pride, riches, oppression of the poor, withheld food and clothing, violence against the humble, mockery of the sacred, denial of prophecy, murder, theft, adultery, contention, and desertion. Boasting in their own strength, they were left in it.

verses.label: v. 14–17
verses.title: Preaching and repentance
verses.text: Moronihah preaches, and so do Nephi and Lehi, sons of Helaman, prophesying what will come without repentance. The people repent and begin to prosper. Seeing it, Moronihah ventures to lead them from city to city until half the property and half the lands are regained.

verses.label: v. 18–20
verses.title: The advance stops
verses.text: In the sixty-second year Moronihah can gain no more. The Lamanites are too numerous, so the plan for the rest is abandoned and the armies hold what they have. The Nephites live in fear of being overpowered and destroyed.

verses.label: v. 21–26
verses.title: What they saw
verses.text: They remember the prophecies of Alma and the words of Mosiah, and see that they had been stiffnecked, had set the commandments at naught, had altered the laws of Mosiah, and had corrupted their law. The church dwindles, prophecy is disbelieved, and the judgments of God stare them in the face. The Spirit no longer preserves them, since it does not dwell in unholy temples, and they see that the Lamanites now match them man for man.

chapter.title: The enemy is made of former members
chapter.text: Verse 8 credits the loss of the land southward to Nephite dissenters leading Lamanite armies. The chapter opens with dissension in the church and closes with the consequences.

chapter.title: The first recruitment attempt failed
chapter.text: Verse 3 has the Lamanites refusing out of fear. Two years of persuasion changed that, and Mormon records both the failure and the success.

chapter.title: Mormon gives the cause before the recovery
chapter.text: Verses 11 through 13 interrupt the campaign narrative to explain it. The military account resumes in verse 14 with preaching.

chapter.title: The list of sins is mostly economic and social
chapter.text: Oppression of the poor, withheld food and clothing, and violence against the humble come before murder and theft in verse 12.

chapter.title: Being left in your own strength is the judgment
chapter.text: Verse 13 makes the boast its own penalty. Nothing is added; what was claimed is simply granted.

chapter.title: Repentance precedes the counterattack
chapter.text: Verse 16 has Moronihah waiting to see repentance before venturing. The record ties the recovery of half the land to it directly.

chapter.title: The recovery stops at half
chapter.text: Verses 18 and 19 have the campaign abandoned for lack of numbers. Mormon reports the limit plainly and has the armies hold rather than press.

chapter.title: The advantage is gone
chapter.text: Verse 26 says Lamanite and Nephite strength are equal, man for man, and dates the change to the space of not many years.

applications.title: Count the people you drive out
applications.text: The exiles became the argument that brought an army. Removing someone from a group does not remove them from the situation.

applications.title: Check whether the failure list is about strength
applications.text: Mormon explains a lost war with food withheld from the hungry. When something collapses, the causes may sit far from where the collapse showed up.

applications.title: Do not let the boast become the plan
applications.text: They trusted their own strength and were given exactly that. Notice where your confidence has quietly replaced your preparation.

applications.title: Wait for the change before the push
applications.text: Moronihah moved only after he saw repentance. Timing an effort to a real shift beats timing it to your own impatience.

questions.text: What conflict of mine started inside the group rather than outside it?
What have I blamed on circumstance that belongs to conduct?
Who is hungry or cold near me while I am comfortable?
What am I boasting in that I would not want to be left alone with?
What began to improve the moment I actually changed?
What have I rightly abandoned, and what have I abandoned too early?
What in me is an unholy temple right now?

entries.head: Hel. 3:36

anchor.quote: because of the pride of their hearts, because of their exceeding riches

entries.reason: the pride growing daily out of riches, two years earlier

targets.quote: the exceedingly great pride which had gotten into the hearts of the people;
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that the fifty and second year ended in peace also, save it were the exceedingly great pride which had gotten into the hearts of the people; and it was because of their exceedingly great riches and their prosperity in the land; and it did grow upon them from day to day.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that the fifty and second year ended in peace also, save it were **the exceedingly great pride which had gotten into the hearts of the people**; and it was because of their exceedingly great riches and their prosperity in the land; and it did grow upon them from day to day.

targets.verse_text: For as their laws and their governments were established by the voice of the people, and they who chose evil were more numerous than they who chose good, therefore they were ripening for destruction, for the laws had become corrupted.
targets.markdown: For as their laws and their governments were established by the voice of the people, and **they who chose evil were more numerous than they who chose good**, therefore they were ripening for destruction, for the laws had become corrupted.
